title: New airliner sets record flying 24 hrs nonstop from Australia to France
gist: The Airbus A350-1000ULR flew 24 hours 25 minutes and 12,460 nautical miles from Melbourne to Toulouse, validating Qantas's Project Sunrise Sydney–New York/London nonstops that go on sale in 2027 with 238 seats and over 40 percent premium cabin allocation. The economics are threatened by jet fuel: airlines face an extra $100 billion fuel bill in 2026 amid the US-Israeli war with Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption, with Singapore Airlines already posting its first quarterly loss since 2022.

insights.claim: The Airbus A350-1000ULR flew 24 hours 25 minutes nonstop from Melbourne to Toulouse covering 12,460 nautical miles, well beyond the roughly 10,000 nautical miles needed for Sydney to London or New York.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Demonstrated range margin removes the main technical risk from Qantas's 2027 ultra-long-haul launch.
insights.locator: That set the stage for the likely record-breaking return flight

insights.claim: The A350-1000ULR carries an extra rear center fuel tank holding 20,900 liters, extending range by 1,000 nautical miles specifically to enable the Qantas routes.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The range unlock is a bolt-on tank rather than a new airframe, so competitors could replicate the capability quickly.
insights.locator: To handle such ultra long-range flights, Airbus describes the aircraft

insights.claim: Qantas has ordered a dozen A350-1000ULRs for Project Sunrise and aims to start selling tickets in 2027 for nonstop Sydney to New York or London service.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A concrete 12-aircraft order and a datable 2027 revenue start for the ultra-long-haul premium experiment.
insights.locator: The Airbus A350-1000ULR was developed specifically

insights.claim: Qantas expects a maximum Project Sunrise commercial flight time of 21 hours 40 minutes, which would beat Singapore Airlines' current Guinness record for longest scheduled nonstop flight of roughly 18 to 19 hours on the A350-900ULR.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Direct competitive displacement of Singapore Airlines' marquee ultra-long-haul franchise.
insights.locator: By comparison, Qantas Airways expects the maximum Project Sunrise flight time

insights.claim: Each Qantas aircraft will carry up to 238 passengers, described as the lowest seat density of any A350-1000 in service in the world, with self-serve food stations and a wellbeing zone using the freed space.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Low density means the route only works on yield, not volume; RASK per premium seat is the metric that matters.
insights.quote: lowest seat density of any A350-1000 in service in the world

insights.claim: Qantas is allocating more than 40 percent of Project Sunrise seats to First, Business and Premium Economy, an explicit bet that premium fares offset the lower total passenger count.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The whole business case rests on sustained premium long-haul demand; a corporate travel downturn breaks it.
insights.quote: Qantas is allocating more than 40 percent of seats to passengers paying higher prices for First, Business, and Premium economy tickets
insights.locator: Ticket prices have not yet been announced

insights.claim: Singapore Airlines' comparable A350-900ULR ultra-long-haul aircraft carries up to 161 passengers on 18-to-19-hour New York to Singapore flights, setting the density benchmark Qantas is deliberately undercutting.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Comparable-route economics from Singapore Airlines are the only real-world proxy for whether Project Sunrise can be profitable.
insights.locator: For now, Singapore Airlines currently offers the longest nonstop

insights.claim: Airlines face the prospect of paying an extra $100 billion on jet fuel in 2026 alone, an industry-wide cost shock independent of any single carrier's operations.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A $100 billion incremental fuel bill compresses global airline margins and is the dominant sector variable for 2026.
insights.quote: Airlines are already facing the prospect of paying an extra $100 billion on jet fuel in 2026 alone
insights.locator: However, Qantas may also consider charging higher ticket prices

insights.claim: Singapore Airlines recently reported its first quarterly net loss since the height of the pandemic in 2022, partly because of soaring jet fuel prices.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The best-run ultra-long-haul operator is already loss-making on fuel, a direct read-through to Project Sunrise economics.
insights.locator: with Singapore Airlines recently reporting its first quarterly net loss

insights.claim: Elevated jet fuel costs are attributed to the US-Israeli war with Iran and ongoing disruptions to oil tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, which may push Qantas to raise ticket prices in 2027.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Hormuz shipping flow is the transmission channel from Middle East conflict to airline P&L and ticket pricing.
insights.locator: However, Qantas may also consider charging higher ticket prices

insights.claim: Airbus test pilot Xavier Pepin describes four-hour shifts per pilot rotated every two hours so incoming and outgoing pilots overlap, a fatigue-management design that ultra-long-haul commercial operations will need to replicate.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Crew scheduling and rest-compartment design are the operational cost drivers that regulators will scrutinize for 20-plus-hour flights.
insights.quote: To manage fatigue during the 20 to 23-hour flights we implemented four-hour shifts for each pilot, but we rotated the crew every two hours
insights.locator: The aircraft also features a twin flight crew rest compartment

insights.claim: Two Qantas pilots already qualified on the A350 joined the return test flight to get first experience with the -1000ULR variant, indicating crew-certification work is running in parallel with aircraft testing.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Parallel crew qualification reduces the lag between aircraft delivery and revenue service.

insights.claim: More than 3.6 million people tracked the return flight on Flightradar24, making it the second-most-tracked flight ever behind the 2022 flight carrying Queen Elizabeth II's coffin.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Free global marketing at a scale airlines rarely buy; supports premium-brand pricing power for the route launch.
